Cards

Both counting methods give the same total, oxidation state and dⁿ; they differ in what each ligand gives. Answer choices are at least 2 apart on Easy and next to each other on Hard; changing the level deals another card. Geometry hides the structure: guess the shape from the number of ligands and the electron count. In the Ligands set, the other choices ask for the L/X class. A card is mastered after two correct answers in a row; progress is saved in this browser. Not mastered leaves out the cards you have mastered in Learn (in Name it, the complexes you named right last time). Star a card ☆, or drag it onto My cards, to keep it in your own set.

Sets

Named complexes

Complexes with a common name, from every set. On Hard the wrong answers come from the same family.

Periodic table, d block

The group number is the electron count of the neutral metal (covalent count); dⁿ = group − oxidation state.

Space flips the card. The arrow keys move between cards.
Click a card to open it as a flashcard. Star it ☆, or drag it onto My cards, to add just that one.

Edit your cards

One card per line: name | formula | electron count | note. Formula and note are optional, so name | 18 works too. A ligand takes its L/X class: carbonyl | CO | L. To bring in a Quizlet set, choose Export on Quizlet, keep “Tab” between term and definition and “New line” between rows, and paste it here. Cards named like a built-in complex get its structure, and its oxidation state and tally when the count matches.
